summary: Preserved the candidate's valid NPU MoE reload regression and corrected its concrete reviewed evidence defect: the assigned gfx950 device reports AMD Instinct MI355X, not MI350X. The production fix was already present on the prepared base; no additional source correction was justified.

tests.what_was_measured: Before changing the candidate, its three focused post-process/reload tests passed. A direct torch query reported AMD Instinct MI355X and gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, reproducing the review's mismatch with the committed MI350X record.
On one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), distinct 1408x64 BF16 gate and up tensors were loaded into a 2816x64 fused destination through the actual loader and both halves were independently compared.
After integrating the candidate and correcting its evidence, the three focused regressions still pass.

gpu_execution.evidence: reports/j-672eeae4940a/raw/gpu_loader_after.txt records the one-GPU BF16 loader check and direct AMD Instinct MI355X identity.

remaining_limitations: No Ascend NPU or CANN/torch_npu runtime was available, so actual npu_format_cast and Ascend grouped-matmul behavior were not independently executed.
The reported DeepSeekV3.2 weights were unavailable, so no full Engine or HTTP update_weights_from_disk run established scheduler survival after reload.
The gfx950 fixture validates tensor-loader behavior only; it does not qualify NPU kernels, DeepSeekV3.2 semantics, HTTP transport, or distributed execution.
